data.text: Ana, I heard the procedure is Friday now. Is it because the test showed something dangerous or because Marcus missed medicine?

prior_context.speaker: nurse_elise
prior_context.text: Correct. Avoid NSAIDs. Use acetaminophen if you need something for pain.

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: I am double-checking the active medication list before tomorrow: apixaban 5 milligrams twice daily, metoprolol tartrate 37.5 milligrams twice daily, lisinopril 10 milligrams daily but held tomorrow morning, omeprazole 20 milligrams daily, and magnesium oxide 400 milligrams nightly for the five-night course.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: That matches what I have written down.

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_choi
prior_context.text: This is Dr. Choi. Since I am on weekend backup after the procedure, I only need the clinical handoff: the Friday TEE-guided cardioversion time, the anticoagulation plan, and return precautions if symptoms recur.

prior_context.speaker: nurse_elise
prior_context.text: I will send you the clinical handoff, but not the social-work housing contact since that is not needed for weekend coverage unless the patient cannot be reached through standard channels.

prior_context.speaker: billing_perez
prior_context.text: Prior authorization is cleared for Friday. Marcus, do you want the paper estimate mailed anywhere or portal only?

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: Portal only. Do not mail anything to any shared address right now.

prior_context.speaker: reception_ana
prior_context.text: I am confirming your Friday arrival again: March 13, 11:00 AM, cardiac procedures unit, third floor. Only your chart has the restricted callback note.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: Thank you. If my cell fails tonight, the Cedar Bridge evening desk is the only backup, and the message must stay generic.

prior_context.speaker: reception_ana
prior_context.text: Understood. I will not repeat those details anywhere else.

states.content: Family access to Marcus Reed's information is revoked, and Friday procedure timing should be given only to Marcus. Previously, through Monday, only logistical information (arrival times, where Marcus needs to go, basic transportation instructions) could be shared with Nina, while medication changes, lab results, adherence history, and chart notes were restricted; the clinical reason for schedule changes was also not to be disclosed. Marcus does not want details of his recovery discussed with family, and nurse Jamison agreed to keep family updates within the logistics scope he set. The TEE-guided cardioversion wording is acceptable in Marcus's portal copy but must not be used in family or voicemail messages. Marcus also does not want another patient or another family member to hear his schedule or contact notes, and wants his chart kept separate from other patients' charts. A same-surname caution note has been added to the desk workflow, and his restricted contact note stays on his chart only; reception Ana confirmed that only Marcus Reed's chart has the restricted callback note.

states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control. Because the timing of his Monday-night apixaban dose is uncertain, Dr. Patel is changing the approach from direct cardioversion to TEE-guided cardioversion so a clot can be checked for first while still avoiding an unnecessary delay. The Wednesday, March 11 slot was released, and the Thursday, March 12 slot was taken by an add-on case; the TEE-guided cardioversion is now scheduled for Friday, March 13 at 12:30 PM with 11:00 AM arrival at the cardiac procedures unit on the third floor. Reception Ana has reconfirmed the Friday arrival: March 13, 11:00 AM, cardiac procedures unit, third floor. Scheduler Terry has updated the arrival letter in the portal, and Marcus's own portal copy prep line now says TEE-guided cardioversion. Marcus requests that the procedure slot details be put in the chart. Dr. Patel has reviewed the labs and stated they are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, satisfying the pending-labs condition; full medication history reconciliation remains part of the plan. Dr. Patel instructs that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion, and to continue apixaban exactly as prescribed without missing any further doses. Pharmacist Klein confirms apixaban stays at 5 mg twice daily and Marcus must not stop or skip it on his own unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. The only routine periprocedural hold discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Nurse Jamison is reviewing Marcus Reed's medications exactly as he is taking them right now, to prepare an accurate current medication list. Marcus reported taking ibuprofen a couple of times last week for shoulder pain before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner (apixaban). Dr. Patel has now instructed Marcus to stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs and to use acetaminophen instead if needed, because NSAIDs raise bleeding risk with apixaban. Pharmacist Klein reinforced this: no ibuprofen or naproxen while Marcus is on apixaban. Dr. Patel instructs Marcus to continue apixaban exactly as prescribed and not miss any further doses. Marcus reported he has not missed any morning apixaban doses and no completely missed doses in the last three weeks as far as he remembers; he might have been a few hours late last Monday night when changing locations but still took that pill before bed. Marcus is pretty sure he took his Monday-night apixaban dose, but it was late and he cannot prove the time. Nurse Jamison will document the Monday-night apixaban dose as possibly delayed but not skipped. Marcus does not drink energy drinks.
